questions.question: Cashpor Micro credit is a company that does NOT operate in the most backward districts of _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telangana**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cashpor Micro Credit **does not operate in the most backward districts of Telangana**.
 
• It** primarily operates in states li**ke Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh.
 
• Cashpor Micro Credit is a** non-profit microfinance institution** that focuses on **providing financial services to poor women in rural areas**,
 
 
• particularly in the backward districts of northern and eastern India. 
 
 
 
• The organization's mission is **to empower women by offering small loans for income-generating activities**, thus helping families overcome poverty.
 
• However, **Telangana is not among the states where Cashpor Micro Credit operates.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Microfinance:

 
 
• Microfinance institution provides financial services to low - income individuals.
 
• Microfinance is a basis of financial services for entrepreneurs and small businesses deficient in contact with banking and associated services.
 
• The two key systems for the release of financial services to such customers include ‘relationship-based banking’ for individual entrepreneurs and small businesses along with ‘group-based models’ where several entrepreneurs come together to apply for loans and other services as a group.
 
• Similar to banking operation traditions, microfinance entities are supposed to charge their lender’s interest on loans.
 
• In most cases the so-called interest rates are lower than those charged by normal banks, certain rivals of this concept accuse microfinance entities of creating gain by manipulating the poor people’s money. 
 
• This includes both the consumers and the self-employed.
 
• Microfinance apart from microcredit, the provision of small loans to poor clients also covers many other services.
 
• Micro Finance covers a wide range of services like credit facilities, saving facilities, insurance facilities, remittance, Short duration loans, Fund Transfer and also non-financial services like training, counseling, etc.
 
• Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) in India exist as NGOs (registered as societies or trusts), Section 25 companies and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs).

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India states that the President shall appoint judges of the Supreme Court under his hand and seal after consultation with such of the judges of the Supreme Court as the President may deem necessary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 124(2)**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 124(2) of the Constitution of India states **that the President appoints judges of the Supreme Court under their hand and seal after consulting with other judges
 
• The Article states '**Every Judge of the Supreme Court shall be appointed by the President **by warrant under his hand and seal after consultation with such of the Judges of the Supreme Court and of the High Courts in the States as the President may deem necessary for the purpose and shall hold office until he attains the age of sixty-five years'.
 
• Additionally,** it states that 'Provided that in the case of appointment of a Judge other than the Chief Justice, the Chief Justice of India shall always be consulted**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 120(2)**

 
 
• Article 120(2) of the Indian Constitution pertains to the **language to be used in Parliament**, particularly addressing the use of English and Hindi during parliamentary proceedings.
 
• It specifies that even though Parliament may transact its business in Hindi or English, **English shall continue to be used for all official purposes of Parliament until Parliament provides otherwise by law.**
 
 
 
• **Article 134(2)**
 
 
• **​**It **allows Parliament to grant the Supreme Court the power to hear appeals from High Court judgments, **final orders, or sentences in criminal proceedings. 
 
• It** empowers Parliament to re**gulate the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in criminal cases.
 
 
 
• **Article 142(2)**
 
 
• **​**It **grants powers to Parliament to make laws for the enforcement of any decrees**, orders, or decisions made by the Supreme Court.
 
• Article 142(2) specifically focuses on **Parliament's role** in making laws to provide mechanisms for:
 
 
• Enforcement of the Supreme Court's decisions.
 
• Execution of orders and directions issued by the Supreme Court.

questions.question: In which of the following years Cripps Mission offered Dominion Status to India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1942**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cripps Mission came to India in **1942**__.
 
• Stafford Cripps was a labour minister in Winston Churchill's coalition government in Britain.
 
• The Cripps Mission came to India from **22 March to 11 April 1942.**
 
• Its aim was to obtain Indian cooperation for the British war in the 2ⁿd World war.
 
• **Proposals of Cripps Mission:**
 __
 
• Setting up of an Indian dominion. 
 
• A Constituent Assembly would be formed to frame a new constitution for the country.
 
• India’s defence would be controlled by the British until this new constitution came into force.
 
• The transfer of power and the rights of minorities would be safeguarded by negotiations between the Constituent Assembly and the British government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Reasons for Failure of Cripps Mission**

 
 
• The Cripps Mission failed due to the following reasons:
 
• **Gandhi referred to the Cripps Mission recommendations as a “post-dated cheque**” because they didn’t appease Indian nationalists and ultimately proved to be nothing more than a marketing tactic for the US and China.
 
• The INC, **which wanted full independence, thought the measures were too conservative, w**hile the British thought they were too radical.
 
• The Mission was condemned by the Muslim League, the INC, and other Indian groups.
 
• The right of the states to secede was contested by both the Liberals and the Hindu Mahasabha.
 
• The Depressed Classes objected since they were worried about their status in a nation in which they would be a minority.
 
• **Viceroy Linlithgow, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Secretary of State for India Leo Amery are also said to have been unsupportive of the mission, **which is another reason it is believed to have failed.
 
• The** British motives were questioned by the justification that the measures were meant to complement the August Offer instead of replacing it.**
 
• The standoff was made worse by Cripps’ refusal to stray from the Draft Declaration and his rigid “take it or leave it” attitude.

questions.question: Which syndrome causes a cartoon character to have a plump face, a fair complexion, and pink or beryl banana marks on the skin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cushing syndrome**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The syndrome that c**auses a cartoon character-like appearance **with a plump face, a fair complexion, and pink or beryl banana marks on the skin is **Cushing syndrome.**
 
• **It is caused by prolonged exposure to high levels of the hormone cortisol, either due to endogenous factors (e.g., adrenal gland overactivity) or exogenous factors (e.g., long-term use of corticosteroids).**
 
• **It is associated with **Weak muscles, high blood pressure, and sometimes a "buffalo hump" (fat pad on the upper back).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marfan syndrome****​**

 
 
• Marfan syndrome affects the heart, eyes, blood vessels, and bones.
 
• People with Marfan syndrome are tall and thin with long arms, legs, fingers, and toes.
 
• Marfan syndrome is an inherited disorder that affects connective tissue.
 
• The fibers that support and anchor your organs and other structures in your body.
 
• Marfan syndrome is caused by a mutation in a gene called FBN1.
 
• The mutation limits the body's ability to make proteins needed to build connective tissue.
 
• A person with Marfan syndrome has a 1 in 2 chance of passing it on to their child.
 
 
 
• Angelman Syndrome
 
 
• **Angelman Syndrome** is a rare genetic disorder that primarily affects the nervous system and is characterized by developmental delays, neurological problems, and unique physical and behavioral traits.
 
• It d**elayed milestones such as sitting, walking, and speech development.**
 
• Individuals with Angelman Syndrome require lifelong care and support. 
 
 
 
• Down's Syndrome
 
 
• Down's Syndrome is the name of the disorder caused by the presence of an extra chromosome.
 
• Down's syndrome is a genetic disorder caused when abnormal cell division results in extra genetic material from chromosome 21.

questions.question: After independence, who had complete control over the established industries?
questions.solution:

__
 
• After India gained independence from the British Raj in 1947, **the government had complete control over established industries.**
 
• The **government took control of industries that were vital to the economy and the public**, such as coal, petroleum, aviation, and steel.
 
• The government **also established new undertakings in six basic industries. **
 
• **The government strictly regulated **the economy through a **system of licenses.**
 
 
• To open a new industry or expand production, a license from the government was required.
 
• This system was known as the "Licence Raj". 
 
 
 
• India **chose a path of economic self-reliance**, which included restricting imports and limiting foreign investment. 
 
• This **approach had many supporters, but also some critics.**
 
• **The Licence Raj protected local businesses but also slowed growth and stifled innovation. **
 
• **In the 1980s, India began to liberalize its economy, loosening restrictions on business creation and import controls. **
 
• **These reforms led to an increase in the average GDP growth rate. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The first industrial policy statement of India is known as Industrial Policy Resolution.
 
• It was announced in the year 1948.
 
• It defined the role of the State in industrial development both as an entrepreneur and authority.
 
• Industrial Policy Resolution,1948 states that India is going to have a Mixed Economic Model.
 
• The Industries (Development and Regula­tion) Act was passed in 1951.
 
• It was passed to implement the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948.

 __

• She was a trailblazer in providing education for girls and for ostracized portions of society.
 
• She opened a school for girls with her husband, Jyotirao Phule.
 
• They found one of the first modern Indian girls' schools in Pune at Bhide Wada.
 
• Savitribai Phule even worked to abolish discrimination and unfair treatment of people based on caste and gender.

questions.question: What type of earthquake occurs when induced stresses around mine workings cause massive rocks to fly explosively from the mine face, creating seismic waves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Collapse earthquake**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A collapse earthquake **occurs when **induced stresses around mine workings cause massive rocks to fly explosively from the mine face**, creating seismic waves
 
• In the areas of intense mining activity, sometimes the roofs of underground mines collapse causing minor tremors.
 
 
• These are called collapse earthquakes.
 
 
 
• They are small earthquakes in underground caverns and mines that are caused by seismic waves produced from the explosion of rock on the surface.
 
• This happens when the induced stress around the mine working because large masses of rock to fly off the mine face explosively, producing seismic waves. 
 
• Collapse earthquakes are also produced by massive land sliding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Tectonic

 earthquakes
 
 
 
• They are the most common earthquake found all over the world.
 
• These are generated due to the sliding of rocks along a fault plane.
 
• It is caused by the movement of plates when energy accumulated within plate boundary zones is released.
 
• Tectonic earthquakes are usually larger than volcanic earthquakes.
 
 
 
 

 Volcanic

 earthquakes
 
 
 
• A special class of tectonic earthquakes is sometimes recognized as a volcanic earthquake. However, these are confined to areas of active volcanoes.
 
• Volcanic earthquakes have different characteristics from the deep and tectonic seismic events that occur along great faults.
 
• They are considerably less devastating and may continue at a detectable level for weeks or months before the eruption.
 
• It is caused by the sudden opening of channels in crustal rocks, rapid changes of motion of magma, excessive accumulation of gas pressure in the crust, roof collapses of subterranean channels emptied of magma.
 
 
 
 

 Explosion
 earthquakes
 
 
 
• Ground shaking may also occur due to the explosion of chemical or nuclear devices. Such tremors are called explosion earthquakes.
 
• Some underground nuclear explosions fired since the 1950s have produced substantial earthquakes.
 
• When a nuclear device is detonated in a borehole underground, enormous nuclear energy is released.

• I. It promotes economic efficiency:
 
 
• This **statement is Correct**
 
• Privatisation** often leads to increased economic efficiency because private entities are motivated by profit** and tend to allocate resources more efficiently than public enterprises.
 
• Competition among private players encourages innovation, better services, and cost-effectiveness.
 
 

 
• II. It delimits the interference of bureaucracy:

__
 
• In the context of globalization, **PPP** stands for **Purchasing Power Parity**.
 
• **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP):**
 
 
• It is an economic **theory used to compare the relative value of currencies** by examining the cost of a standard basket of goods and services in different countries
 
• The PPP **exchange rate helps determine the purchasing power of one country's currency relative to another's.**
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• If a product costs ₹50 in India and $1 in the United States, the PPP exchange rate would be 1 USD = 50 INR, assuming the product basket is identical.
 
• Organizations like the World Bank and IMF frequently use PPP-adjusted metrics to analyze global economies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__Concept of Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) and its implications:__

 
• Role of PPP: ​​

 
 
• ​The PPP is **used as a measure to compare the economic productivity** and standards of living between countries.
 
• This is particularly **useful in international economic studies**, where one needs to compare economies with different currencies.
 
 
 
• Absolute vs. Relative PPP: 
 
 
• **Absolute PPP suggests t**hat the exchange rate between two currencies reflects the cost of a similar basket of goods in both countries.
 
• **Relative PPP, on the other hand, takes into consideration the rate of inflation, **suggesting that the rate of appreciation or depreciation of a currency would be equal to the difference in inflation rates between two countries.
 
 
 
• Other Assumptions: 
 
 
• ​Aside from no transaction costs, no transportation costs, and free movement of goods (trading without tariffs or quotas), **another implicit assumption of PPP includes that the goods are homogeneous or identical across different markets.**
 
 
 
• Limitations of PPP: 
 
 
• **​​In real-world scenarios**, the PPP seldom holds due to transportation and conversion costs, trade barriers, differences in taxation, and the existence of goods and services that aren't available in all countries.
 
• Besides, this theory often falters because it overlooks the market segmentation and differentiation of products between countries.
 
 
 
• PPP and Exchange Rates: 
 
 
• ​**Central banks and economists often use PPP when assessing the fair value of a currency. **

The correct answer is 84. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Lok Sabha considered as the lower house.
 
• It has seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Tribes.
 
• As per the order issued by the** Delimitation Commission in 2008,** **412 are general, 84 seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and 47 seats for the Scheduled Tribes .**
 
• The number of seats reserved for scheduled tribes was increased from 79 to 84 in the 15th Lok Sabha elections.
 
• The maximum strength of the House envisaged by the Constitution is 552.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 131 seats out of the 543 Lok Sabha seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
 
• This is approximately 24% of all the seats.
 
• 84 seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes, and 47 seats are reserved for Scheduled Tribes.
 
• These numbers are changed by the Delimitation Commission of India based on changes in the population.
 
• By-election of up to 530 members to represent the States, up to 20 members to represent the Union Territories and two members of the Anglo-Indian Community to be nominated by the Hon'ble President. which was removed by 104th constitutional Amendment Act.

questions.question:
Below are some statements about the Ozone layer.

**Statement 1.** It is found in the stratosphere.

**Statement 2.** Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are responsible for Ozone hole.

**Statement 3.** Ozone layer is found around 15–30 km above the earth’s surface.

**Statement 4. **Ozone layer is expected not to recover anymore now.

Which of these statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statements 1, 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ozone layer is indeed found in the **stratosphere**, which is the second major layer of Earth's atmosphere, just above the troposphere and below the mesosphere.
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons **(CFCs) are responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer, leading to the formation of the **ozone hole**.
 
• The ozone layer is located approximately **15-30 km above the Earth's surface**, which helps protect living organisms by filtering out harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun.
 
• Statement 4 is incorrect because recent studies have shown that the** ozone layer is slowly recovering due to the global reduction in the use of CFCs** and other ozone-depleting substances, primarily due to the Montreal Protocol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone Layer**

 
 
• The ozone layer is a high concentration of ozone (O₃) molecules located in the stratosphere, about 15 to 30 kilometers above the Earth's surface.
 
• It plays a crucial role in absorbing the majority of the sun’s harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation, particularly UV-B and UV-C rays, which can cause skin cancer and cataracts in humans and are harmful to marine life and plants.
 
 
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**
 
 
• CFCs are man-made chemical compounds that were commonly used in air conditioning, refrigeration, and as propellants in aerosol sprays.
 
• When CFCs are released into the atmosphere, they eventually reach the stratosphere, where they are broken down by UV radiation, releasing chlorine atoms which then deplete ozone molecules.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol**
 
 
• The Montreal Protocol is an international treaty designed to phase out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances (ODS), including CFCs, halons, and other related chemicals.
 
• It was agreed upon on **September 16, 1987**, and has been ratified by all 197 UN member countries, making it one of the most successful environmental agreements in history.
 
• Thanks to the Montreal Protocol, the ozone layer is expected to recover to 1980 levels by the middle of the 21st century.
 
 
 
• **Stratosphere**
 
 
• The stratosphere is the second layer of the Earth's atmosphere, situated above the troposphere and below the mesosphere.
 
• It extends from about **10 km to 50 km **above the Earth's surface.
 
• The stratosphere contains the ozone layer, which absorbs and scatters ultraviolet solar radiation.

questions.question: Hojagiri is a famous dance form of which of these states?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "__**Tripura**__". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Hojagiri** is a folk dance performed in the state of **Tripura** by the **Reang people.**
 
• **Reang** is one of the** 21 scheduled tribes** of the Indian state of **Tripura**.
 
• The dance is performed by women and young girls, about** 4 to 6 members in a team,** singing, balancing on an earthen pitcher, and managing other props such as a bottle on the head and earthen lamp on the hand, while only the lower half of the body is moved.
 
• It is attractive due to its melodious songs accompanied by bamboo flute, cymbals, and the khamb.
 
• The dance is performed during the Hojagiri festival or **Laxmi** **Puja** held on the following full moon night of **Durga Puja, generally** after** 3rd day of Dashera.**
 
• The **Goddess Mailuma, (Laxmi)** is worshipped on this day.
 
• The whole of the **Huk or Jhum cultivatio**n is exhibited through this **dance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/03e5179c9b764988d9e21f589aa7e75fc8b01d08fe4a8276bbd94ca535226a15.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
